html:
Serbia is a country in the central Balkans, with its capital at Belgrade. The map shows it in three lives: the medieval principality and kingdom from 900 to 1279, the modern kingdom from 1880 to 1914, and the state left after the breakup of Yugoslavia in 1994 and 2010.

Serbs arrived with the other Slavs who settled the Balkans in the 600s. Their princes took Christianity from Constantinople in the 800s and lived in the shadow of Byzantium and Bulgaria.

The medieval high point:

  • Stefan Nemanja, from about 1166, united the Serb lands and founded the Nemanjić dynasty.
  • His son Stefan became king in 1217, and another son, Saint Sava, won the Serbian church its own head in 1219.
  • Monasteries such as Studenica were built and painted.
  • Stefan Dušan crowned himself emperor in 1346 and issued Dušan's Code.

After the Battle of Kosovo in 1389 Serbia slid under the Ottoman Empire, which took the last stronghold in 1459. In 1690 many Serbs fled north in the Great Migration.

Revolts from 1804 won self-rule, and the Congress of Berlin recognised full independence in 1878. The killing of the Austrian heir in Sarajevo by a Bosnian Serb in 1914 set off the First World War. In 1918 Serbia became the core of Yugoslavia. When Yugoslavia broke up in the 1990s, Serbia fought wars with its neighbours and stayed in a union with Montenegro until 2006. Kosovo declared independence in 2008, which Serbia does not accept.
